title: Resource Friction Playbook — cost savings pipeline for inference workloads
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Create a practical, cross-team playbook and rollout pipeline to capture predictable cost savings from inference-level optimizations (dynamic batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles) and embed them into product roadmaps and runbooks. The deliverable is a staged program: 1) discovery + benchmark matrix across representative workloads, 2) a set of prioritized, runnable experiments with expected ROI, 3) integration points for Console (reporting + rollout toggles), and 4) a handoff template for Dedicated/Private onboarding. This ticket tracks the PM-level initiative, coordination with Eng/Design, and OKR mapping.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark corpus covering 6 representative customer workloads with token-distribution histograms and baseline p50/p95 latency and cost-per-1k-token metrics
A prioritized experiment backlog with runbooks for 12 independent experiments (4 batching, 4 caching, 4 quantization) including success metrics and estimated unit-econ impact
Console prototype that surfaces per-route estimated cost savings and an operator toggle for safe canary rollout
Validated rollout runbook and checklist for Dedicated and Private customers including KMS/compatibility notes
Initial OKR targets: 15% average unit-cost reduction for low-latency routes and 25% opportunity capture for batchy workloads by EOY
decisions: Use a common benchmark harness (open-source + internal telemetry) rather than ad-hoc customer traces to ensure comparability
Classify experiments into 'safe-lift' (no user-visible change) and 'repro-profile' (requires model/regression checks) to speed adoption
Prioritize batching/caching experiments on p50-sensitive routes and quantization on bulk embedding workloads
Expose rollout toggles in Console before automating auto-rollout; require one manual canary per tenant
